title: July 2026 expense difficulty and institution-specific confidence diverge by group
source_unit: US Census Bureau HTOPS/HPS July 2026 public-use person respondent, stratified by recent household expense difficulty

observations.period: July 15–August 3, 2026; no difficulty paying usual expenses

denominator.unit: unweighted valid respondents for federal-statistics confidence; item-specific Congress denominator is 7148

observations.method: PWEIGHT/PWEIGHT0 weighted descriptive shares with 80 successive-difference replicate weights; no difficulty is EXPENSE_DIFFICULT=1 and high confidence is response 1 or 2.
observations.uncertainty: Cross-sectional design-based replicate standard errors; no timing, causal, or attrition inference.
observations.subgroup: Respondents reporting no difficulty with usual household expenses; outcome-specific valid universes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Confidence can reflect prior identity, institutional experience, information, or nonfinancial conditions rather than current expense difficulty.

observations.period: July 15–August 3, 2026; at least a little difficulty paying usual expenses

denominator.unit: unweighted valid respondents for federal-statistics confidence; item-specific Congress denominator is 4277

observations.method: Same July PWEIGHT/PWEIGHT0 and 80-replicate procedure; any difficulty is EXPENSE_DIFFICULT in {2,3,4}.
observations.uncertainty: Cross-sectional design-based replicate standard errors; the expense item covers the prior two months and does not identify a specific event.
observations.subgroup: Respondents reporting at least a little difficulty with usual household expenses; outcome-specific valid universes.
observations.counterinterpretation: A respondent can report expense difficulty and retain confidence in one institution; the comparison does not measure political action or generalized distrust.

denominator.unit: two disjoint expense-difficulty groups; outcome-specific valid cases

expense_difficulty_minus_no_difficulty_f.unit: percentage points; replicate-difference SE 1.9537; approximate 90% interval -18.3350 to -11.9073

expense_difficulty_minus_no_difficulty_c.unit: percentage points; replicate-difference SE 1.7548; approximate 90% interval -9.8286 to -4.0554

observations.method: Difference of the two group estimates calculated within each of the 80 replicate weights, followed by the Census successive-difference variance formula.
observations.uncertainty: The intervals describe sampling/design uncertainty for a same-round descriptive contrast. They do not establish that expense difficulty changed confidence.
observations.subgroup: Expense-difficulty contrast, with federal statistical agencies and Congress retained as separate institutional outcomes.
observations.counterinterpretation: The relationship can reflect common causes, prior trust, party identity, reporting differences, or the fact that both measures are contemporaneous.

related_sources.claim: March–May–July 2026 HTOPS/HPS cross-sectional comparison supplies the period context and subgroup layers.
Reproduction audit preserves input hashes, classifications, valid counts, and replicate calculations.

boundary: This is a replicate-weighted same-round cross-sectional association. It does not establish a dated material-to-trust pathway, institutional blame, generalized distrust, political action, recovery, or causality.
